description: Percona ClusterSync for MongoDB (PCSM): health of the source cluster, the sync and the target cluster side by side, then replication progress and pipeline, then detailed health of the PCSM instances.

options.content:
### How to use this dashboard

Work from top to bottom and stop as soon as everything is green. Hover the **ⓘ** icon on any panel: it says what the panel shows, what normal looks like, and what to check if it is not.

| Section | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| **1 · Is the migration healthy?** | Source, ClusterSync and target side by side. Red or yellow tiles show where to look. |
| **2 · Is replication progressing?** | Initial clone progress, then the lag against the source oplog window. |
| **3 · Why is replication slow or stuck?** *(collapsed)* | Where events pile up in the PCSM pipeline. Open it when lag grows. |
| **4 · Are the ClusterSync instances healthy?** | Availability, HA roles and process resources of each PCSM instance. |

**Healthy looks like:** Members Down is 0 on both sides · exactly one ACTIVE instance · replication lag under 10 s and flat · Applied keeps pace with Read and the queues in section 3 stay near 0 · the source oplog window stays far above the lag · target disk below 80%.

**Finding the bottleneck (section 3):** dispatcher queue growing → workers cannot take events fast enough · worker or bulk queues growing with rising flush duration → the target is slow to accept writes · one worker far above the others → a hot collection or document.

**Setup checklist** — most empty panels come from one of these:
1. Pick the **Source Cluster** and **Target Cluster** at the top. Both must be added to PMM with `--cluster`.
2. For sharded clusters, monitor the shard and config server **mongod** members, not only mongos — oplog and replication panels need them.
3. The PMM monitoring user needs `read` on the `local` database for the oplog window.
4. PCSM **1.0.0 or later** for the HA panels, added to PMM as an external service.

Docs: [Percona ClusterSync for MongoDB](https://docs.percona.com/percona-clustersync-for-mongodb/) · [Add MongoDB to PMM](https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/install-pmm/install-pmm-client/connect-database/mongodb.html) · [Add an external service to PMM](https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/install-pmm/install-pmm-client/connect-database/external.html)

panels.description:
Source cluster members (mongod and mongos) that PMM reports as down.

**Normal:** 0.

**If not:** Open ReplSet Summary or Sharded Cluster Summary for the source (header links) to see which member is down. A source member outage can stop or slow the sync.
panels.title: Members Down

panels.description:
Highest CPU utilization among the hosts that run source cluster members.

**Normal:** Below 70%, and no jump when the sync starts.

**If not:** PCSM reads put load on the source. If the source is saturated, the initial clone slows down and production traffic may suffer; consider running the clone off-peak.

Needs node_exporter on the hosts, so it is not available for remotely monitored or DBaaS clusters such as MongoDB Atlas.

targets.expr: max((1 - avg by (node_name) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle"}))) and on (node_name) mongodb_up{cluster="$source_cluster"})

panels.title: Max Node CPU

panels.description:
Smallest oplog window among the source cluster members: how far back the oplog reaches.

**Normal:** Hours or more, well above the PCSM replication lag and above the expected initial clone duration. Red below 1 hour, yellow below 6 hours.

**If not:** PCSM resumes change replication from the source oplog. If lag or clone time reaches the window, the resume point is lost and the sync must restart. Increase the source oplog size, or reduce the lag (see section 3).

Needs the cluster's mongod members (shard and config server replica set members, not only mongos) monitored with the same cluster label. The PMM monitoring user also needs read on the local database.
panels.title: Oplog Window

panels.description:
Highest replication lag of a secondary within the source cluster. This is the source's own replication, not the PCSM lag.

**Normal:** A few seconds at most; 0 when the replica sets have no secondaries.

**If not:** The source cluster is under stress. Check Source Operations and CPU, and the ReplSet Summary for the source.

Needs the cluster's mongod members (shard and config server replica set members, not only mongos) monitored with the same cluster label.
panels.title: Internal Replication Lag

panels.description:
Whether PMM can scrape each PCSM instance (UP / DOWN).

**Normal:** All instances UP.

**If not:** Check the PCSM process and its host (the tile links to Node Summary). An instance that has been unreachable for the whole time range is not listed at all; "unknown" means the host or its pmm-agent is not reporting.
panels.title: Instances Up

panels.description:
The PCSM instance that holds the HA lease (ACTIVE) and runs the sync.

**Normal:** Exactly one instance.

**If not:** "none" means no instance is running the sync: check Instance Availability and Instance Roles in section 4.

Requires PCSM 1.0.0 or later.
panels.title: Active Instance

panels.description:
How far the target is behind the source, in logical seconds, reported by the ACTIVE instance.

**Normal:** Under 10 seconds once change replication runs. It is also 0 before replication has started.

**If not:** Check whether events are read faster than they are applied (Change Events Rate), then look for the bottleneck in section 3.
panels.title: Replication Lag

panels.description:
Remaining logical seconds until the initial sync catches up, reported by the ACTIVE instance.

**Normal:** Decreasing during the initial sync. PCSM keeps reporting the last value after the sync completes until the process restarts.

**If not:** If it does not go down, check copy throughput in section 2 and source and target load in this section.
panels.title: Initial Sync Lag

panels.description:
Target cluster members (mongod and mongos) that PMM reports as down.

**Normal:** 0.

**If not:** Open ReplSet Summary or Sharded Cluster Summary for the target (header links). PCSM cannot apply writes to an unavailable target.
panels.title: Members Down

panels.description:
Highest CPU utilization among the hosts that run target cluster members.

**Normal:** Below 70%. It is expected to rise during the initial clone.

**If not:** A saturated target slows down every write PCSM makes. Check Target Operation Latency and consider scaling the target before the migration.

Needs node_exporter on the hosts.

targets.expr: max((1 - avg by (node_name) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle"}))) and on (node_name) mongodb_up{cluster="$target_cluster"})

panels.title: Max Node CPU

panels.description:
Fullest real filesystem among the hosts that run target cluster members, from node_exporter. Falls back to the size MongoDB reports for members without node_exporter (needs the service added with --enable-all-collectors).

**Normal:** Below 80%, with room for the whole source dataset plus indexes.

**If not:** The initial clone copies the whole dataset. Free or add disk space before the target fills up, or the sync fails.

It does not know which mount holds the MongoDB data, so a nearly full disk that MongoDB does not use also shows here.

targets.expr: max((1 - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{fstype!~"rootfs|selinuxfs|autofs|rpc_pipefs|tmpfs|shm|overlay|squashfs|nsfs|devtmpfs|ramfs"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{fstype!~"rootfs|selinuxfs|autofs|rpc_pipefs|tmpfs|shm|overlay|squashfs|nsfs|devtmpfs|ramfs"}) and on (node_name) mongodb_up{cluster="$target_cluster"}) or max(max by (service_name) (mongodb_dbstats_fsUsedSize{cluster="$target_cluster"}) / max by (service_name) (mongodb_dbstats_fsTotalSize{cluster="$target_cluster"}))

panels.title: Disk Space Used

panels.description:
Highest replication lag of a secondary within the target cluster. This is the target's own replication, not the PCSM lag.

**Normal:** A few seconds at most; 0 when the replica sets have no secondaries.

**If not:** Target secondaries cannot keep up with the PCSM write load, which slows down majority writes and therefore the sync. Check target CPU and disk.

Needs the cluster's mongod members (shard and config server replica set members, not only mongos) monitored with the same cluster label.
panels.title: Internal Replication Lag

panels.description:
Operations per second on the source cluster, summed across members.

**Normal:** Production traffic plus PCSM reads (queries, getmores) during the clone. Source writes are the changes PCSM must replicate.

**If not:** A write rate higher than Change Events Rate (Applied) can sustain makes the lag grow.
panels.title: Operations

panels.description:
Average operation latency of the slowest source member, by operation type.

**Normal:** No lasting rise when the sync starts.

**If not:** A rise that starts with the sync means PCSM is affecting production on the source; consider scheduling the clone off-peak.
panels.title: Operation Latency

panels.description:
Replication lag and initial-sync lag of the ACTIVE instance over time.

**Normal:** Initial-sync lag trends to 0 during the clone; replication lag then stays flat and low.

**If not:** A steadily growing line means PCSM cannot keep up: compare Read and Applied in Change Events Rate, then check section 3. Sudden spikes often line up with a failover (section 4).
panels.title: Lag Time

panels.description:
Change events read from the source and applied to the target per second by the ACTIVE instance.

**Normal:** Applied keeps pace with Read. Both are 0 while the source has no writes or the initial clone is running.

**If not:** A gap alone is not a backlog: PCSM counts every change stream event as read, but skips some without counting them as applied (replayed events, excluded namespaces) and counts bulk writes by operation. If the gap keeps widening while the lag and the queues in section 3 grow, the target cannot keep up: check Target Operation Latency. Read far below the source write rate means reading from the source is slow.
panels.title: Change Events Rate

panels.description:
Operations per second on the target cluster, summed across members.

**Normal:** During a migration the writes here come mostly from PCSM.

**If not:** If writes stop while the lag grows, PCSM is not applying: check sections 3 and 4.
panels.title: Operations

panels.description:
Average operation latency of the slowest target member, by operation type.

**Normal:** Stable. Some increase during the initial clone is expected.

**If not:** High write latency is the most common reason the lag grows. Check target CPU, disk and Internal Replication Lag.
panels.title: Operation Latency

panels.description:
Share of the estimated data size already inserted into the target by the ACTIVE instance.

**Normal:** Grows towards 100% during the initial clone.

**If not:** If it stalls, check Copy Throughput and source and target load.

Only meaningful during an uninterrupted clone: the counters reset when PCSM restarts or fails over.

targets.expr: max by (service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_copy_insert_size_bytes_total{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} unless on(service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_ha_active{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} == 0)) / max by (service_name) ((percona_clustersync_mongodb_estimated_total_size_bytes{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} unless on(service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_ha_active{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} == 0)) > 0)

panels.title: Copy Progress

panels.description:
Bytes inserted into the target during the initial clone, against the estimated total size (ACTIVE instance).

**Normal:** Inserted climbs towards the estimated total.

**If not:** A flat Inserted line during the clone means the copy is stuck: check Batch Duration and the target.

The copy counters belong to each PCSM process, so an instance that became ACTIVE after a restart or failover shows no clone data.

defaults.noValue: No clone data in this process

panels.title: Copied vs Estimated Size

panels.description:
Bytes per second read from the source and inserted into the target during the initial clone (ACTIVE instance).

**Normal:** Read and Insert stay close together at a steady rate.

**If not:** Low read throughput points to the source or the network; Insert well below Read points to the target.

The copy counters belong to each PCSM process, so an instance that became ACTIVE after a restart or failover shows no clone data.

defaults.noValue: No clone data in this process

panels.title: Copy Throughput

panels.description:
Documents per second read from the source and inserted into the target during the initial clone (ACTIVE instance).

**Normal:** Read and Inserted stay close together.

**If not:** See Copy Throughput; many small documents give a high document rate at a low byte rate.

The copy counters belong to each PCSM process, so an instance that became ACTIVE after a restart or failover shows no clone data.

defaults.noValue: No clone data in this process

panels.title: Documents Copied per Second

panels.description:
Duration of the most recent read and insert batch during the initial clone (ACTIVE instance).

**Normal:** Stable.

**If not:** Growing read batches point to the source, growing insert batches to the target.
panels.title: Batch Duration

panels.description:
PCSM lag (ACTIVE instance) against the smallest source oplog window. Logarithmic scale.

**Normal:** The oplog window line stays far above both lag lines.

**If not:** If the lag, or the time since the initial clone started, reaches the oplog window, the change stream resume point is lost and the sync must restart. Increase the source oplog size or reduce the lag.

Needs the cluster's mongod members (shard and config server replica set members, not only mongos) monitored with the same cluster label. The PMM monitoring user also needs read on the local database.
panels.title: Lag vs Source Oplog Window

panels.description:
Events waiting between the change stream reader and the dispatcher that routes them to workers (ACTIVE instance).

**Normal:** Near 0.

**If not:** A growing queue means the workers cannot take events fast enough: check the worker queues and Flush Duration.
panels.title: Dispatcher Queue

panels.description:
Events waiting in the workers' inbound queues (ACTIVE instance): total, and the fullest single worker.

**Normal:** Near 0.

**If not:** If one worker is much fuller than the rest, writes concentrate on few collections or documents (see Per-Worker panels below). If all are full, the target applies too slowly.

Shows 0 until PCSM routes its first change event (during the initial clone, while the source has no writes, or right after a restart or failover).

targets.expr: sum by (service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_repl_worker_event_queue_size{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} unless on(service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_ha_active{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} == 0)) or max by (service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_repl_event_queue_size{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} unless on(service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_ha_active{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} == 0)) * 0

max by (service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_repl_worker_event_queue_size{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} unless on(service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_ha_active{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} == 0)) or max by (service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_repl_event_queue_size{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} unless on(service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_ha_active{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} == 0)) * 0

panels.title: Worker Event Queues

panels.description:
Sealed bulk writes waiting to be written to the target in the workers' async queues (ACTIVE instance): total, and the fullest single worker.

**Normal:** Near 0.

**If not:** Bulks piling up means target writes are the bottleneck: check Flush Duration and Target Operation Latency.

Shows 0 until PCSM routes its first change event.

targets.expr: sum by (service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_repl_worker_bulk_queue_size{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} unless on(service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_ha_active{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} == 0)) or max by (service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_repl_event_queue_size{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} unless on(service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_ha_active{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} == 0)) * 0

max by (service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_repl_worker_bulk_queue_size{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} unless on(service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_ha_active{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} == 0)) or max by (service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_repl_event_queue_size{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} unless on(service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_ha_active{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} == 0)) * 0

panels.title: Worker Bulk Queues

panels.description:
Events applied per second by all replication workers of the ACTIVE instance.

**Normal:** Follows the source write rate.

**If not:** A drop while queues grow means applying to the target has slowed down.

Shows 0 until PCSM routes its first change event.

targets.expr: sum by (service_name) (rate(percona_clustersync_mongodb_repl_worker_events_applied_total{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"}) unless on(service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_ha_active{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} == 0)) or max by (service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_repl_event_queue_size{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} unless on(service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_ha_active{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} == 0)) * 0

panels.title: Worker Events Applied

panels.description:
99th percentile duration of bulk writes to the target, across all workers of the ACTIVE instance.

**Normal:** Stable, typically well under a second.

**If not:** Rising flush duration means the target is slow to accept writes: check target CPU, disk and Internal Replication Lag.

Empty until PCSM flushes its first change-replication bulk write (not during the initial clone, nor while the source has no writes).

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (service_name, le) (rate(percona_clustersync_mongodb_repl_worker_flush_duration_seconds_bucket{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"}) unless on(service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_ha_active{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} == 0)))

panels.title: Flush Duration (p99)

panels.description:
99th percentile number of operations per bulk write, across all workers of the ACTIVE instance.

**Normal:** Larger batches under heavy write load, small ones when the load is light.

**If not:** Batches that stay at the maximum while queues grow mean PCSM is applying as fast as it can and the target is the limit.

Empty until PCSM flushes its first change-replication bulk write.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (service_name, le) (rate(percona_clustersync_mongodb_repl_worker_flush_batch_size_bucket{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"}) unless on(service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_ha_active{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} == 0)))

panels.title: Flush Batch Size (p99)

panels.description:
Top 10 workers by inbound queue size (ACTIVE instance only).

**Normal:** Workers stay close to each other and near 0.

**If not:** One worker far above the rest points to a hot collection or document.
panels.title: Worker Event Queue - $service_name

panels.description:
Top 10 workers by events applied per second (ACTIVE instance only).

**Normal:** Load spread across workers.

**If not:** One busy worker with the rest idle points to a hot collection or document.
panels.title: Worker Events Applied - $service_name

panels.description:
Top 10 workers by p99 bulk write duration (ACTIVE instance only). Workers that did not flush in the interval are not shown.

**Normal:** Similar across workers.

**If not:** One slow worker points to a slow collection on the target, for example one with many indexes.

targets.expr: topk_max(10, histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (worker, le) (rate(percona_clustersync_mongodb_repl_worker_flush_duration_seconds_bucket{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"}) unless on(service_name) (percona_clustersync_mongodb_ha_active{environment=~"$environment",cluster=~"$cluster",service_name=~"$service_name"} == 0))))

panels.title: Worker Flush Duration (p99) - $service_name
3 · Why is replication slow or stuck?

panels.description:
Whether PMM could scrape each PCSM instance over time (UP / DOWN).

**Normal:** UP all the time.

**If not:** Gaps or DOWN periods mean the process, host or pmm-agent was not reporting. Check the host in Node Summary.
panels.title: Instance Availability

panels.description:
Role of each PCSM instance over time: ACTIVE holds the lease and runs the sync, STANDBY waits to take over.

**Normal:** One ACTIVE instance, stable over time.

**If not:** Frequent switches mean the ACTIVE instance keeps losing its lease: check Instance Availability, CPU and memory.

Requires PCSM 1.0.0 or later.
panels.title: Instance Roles

panels.description:
Current HA lease term per cluster (HA group). It increases every time a different instance takes over.

**Normal:** Unchanged during a healthy sync.

**If not:** An increasing term means failovers: see Instance Roles.

Requires PCSM 1.0.0 or later.
panels.title: Lease Term

panels.description:
HA role changes per instance in the selected time range.

**Normal:** 1 for the instance that became ACTIVE at startup, 0 otherwise.

**If not:** More transitions mean failovers: see Instance Roles and the process panels below.

Requires PCSM 1.0.0 or later.
panels.title: Role Transitions

panels.description:
CPU used by each PCSM process (100% = one full core).

**Normal:** Steady; higher during the initial clone.

**If not:** A process pinned at its CPU limit cannot go faster: give it more CPU.
panels.title: CPU Usage

panels.description:
Resident memory (RSS) of each PCSM process.

**Normal:** Stable after the start.

**If not:** Steady growth may lead to an out-of-memory kill and a failover.
panels.title: Resident Memory

panels.description:
Open and maximum file descriptors of each PCSM process.

**Normal:** Open well below Max.

**If not:** Raise the process file descriptor limit before Open reaches Max.
panels.title: File Descriptors

panels.description:
Go runtime goroutines and OS threads of each PCSM process.

**Normal:** Stable.

**If not:** Steady growth points to a leak; report it with the PCSM version.
panels.title: Goroutines and Threads

panels.description:
Go heap memory of each PCSM process.

**Normal:** In use rises and falls with load.

**If not:** Steady growth of In use points to a leak.
panels.title: Go Heap

panels.description:
Median and maximum Go garbage-collection pause of each PCSM process.

**Normal:** Milliseconds.

**If not:** Long pauses stall the sync; usually caused by memory pressure (see Resident Memory).
panels.title: GC Pause Duration
